$comment: Canonical schema for frontline hiring funnel analysis. Every data lane maps into this; scripts/analyze.py reads nothing else. Column names are the contract - an adapter renames source columns into these.

application_id.pii: Must not resolve to a person outside your own systems.

applied_at.unlocks: Time window, seasonality stratification, elapsed-time confound checks.

stage_reached.unlocks: The funnel itself. Without it there is no analysis.

location_id.unlocks: Whether a loss is systemic or concentrated in a handful of sites.

region.unlocks: Configuration differences applied at group level.

hiring_manager_id.unlocks: Manager-level early attrition. Always tested within role.
hiring_manager_id.pii: Must be opaque. A manager is a person.

role.unlocks: Role mix confound. Also a driver in its own right.

source.unlocks: Channel quality, and the single most important confound in this dataset.

commute_band_km.unlocks: Commute effect on first-shift no-shows. Send a band, never an address.

availability_match.unlocks: Whether a screening rule is knocking out available candidates.

screened_at.unlocks: Wait before screening. Part of the capacity-vs-rule distinction.

interview_scheduled_at.unlocks: Scheduling wait - the signature of scarce interview slots.

interview_completed_at.unlocks: Interview no-show rate and the wait that drives it.

scheduled_first_shift_at.unlocks: The offer-to-first-shift gap, usually the largest single no-show driver.

first_shift_at.unlocks: Whether the hire actually turned up. The most expensive loss in the funnel.

exit_reason.unlocks: Mechanism classification: rule / capacity / candidate / quality.

separation_at.unlocks: Early attrition, which turns a hire into a loss after the fact.

separation_reason.unlocks: Whether early leavers are a hiring problem or a job problem.

docs_submitted_at.unlocks: Wait before screening. Part of the capacity-vs-rule distinction.
docs_submitted_at.description: Activation funnel only. Date the sign-up's documents were submitted.

background_clear_at.unlocks: Interview no-show rate and the wait that drives it.
background_clear_at.description: Activation funnel only. Date the background check cleared.

scheduled_first_job_at.unlocks: The offer-to-first-shift gap, usually the largest single no-show driver.
scheduled_first_job_at.description: Activation funnel only. Date the worker was expected to take a first job.

first_job_at.unlocks: Whether the hire actually turned up. The most expensive loss in the funnel.
first_job_at.description: Activation funnel only. Date of the first completed job. Blank means never activated.

refuses.note: If any column name matches or contains one of these, the engine stops and asks for a re-export. Candidate records belong inside your own systems.

stage_profiles.$comment: Two funnel shapes. The engine picks one by matching the values found in stage_reached, and every downstream pass is identical. A W2 hire is interviewed and given an offer; a gig worker is cleared and activated. Nothing else about the analysis differs.

hire.label: Apply to first shift
hire.applies_to: W2 frontline hiring: retail, restaurants and QSR, logistics W2, staffing placement

activation.label: Sign-up to first job
activation.applies_to: Gig and 1099 marketplaces: delivery, courier, rideshare. There is no interview and no offer; the funnel ends at the first completed job, not at a start date.

duration_thresholds.$comment: Thresholds for the cycle-time engine. Separate from 'thresholds', which governs the conversion-rate engine: a rate and a wait are not made unreliable by the same things.
